title: Locally stamped device or master token may be forwarded to connected remote servers
description: Raised by the code review of ticket 8f313dbc; found by reading the code, not reproduced. When indigo_use_host_suffix is false, indigo_change_property in indigo_libs/indigo_bus.c (around line 1011) also routes every change request to the '@ host' remote-server adapter devices. The XML client adapter then writes any nonzero property->access_token into the outgoing request (indigo_libs/indigo_xml.c around line 2007). A request stamped locally with indigo_get_device_or_master_token, for example by config_restore_handler in indigo_libs/indigo_driver.c, by the Configuration Agent replay dispatch added in 8f313dbc or by the indigo_change_*_property helpers, could therefore carry the local device or master token to a connected remote INDIGO server. First step: confirm or refute this with a test that connects a server to a second server and inspects the forwarded request. If confirmed, decide with the owner where the token should be dropped; this touches the bus/adapter trust boundary, hence the full profile. Severity is unknown until the behaviour is confirmed.

outcome.summary: Bus change itself is correct and matches option A: has_host_suffix (indigo_libs/indigo_bus.c:1001-1004) matches exactly the names indigo_xml.c builds on receive ('%s %s' with the adapter name, indigo_xml.c:593 and the other set/def handlers) and is consistent with the strrchr('@') strip on send (indigo_xml.c:1999-2006), including chained names 'X @ upstream @ host'; boundaries (name equal to or shorter than the adapter name, no space before '@', adapter names with spaces) are handled; the suffix-off pre-scan (indigo_bus.c:1012-1018) is a bounded O(MAX_DEVICES=256) strcmp pass under the already held device_mutex with no callbacks, empty names keep broadcasting, '@'-names are excluded from the scan, remote-only names keep reaching adapters, prop_tool (no local devices) and indigo_server chains behave as before apart from L1/L3. New unit cases are sound: they would fail on the old routing (strstr matches '@ host' in 'X @ host:7625' and '@ indigo' in 'X @ indigosky'; suffix off broadcast to '@ Remote'), assertions are inside helpers so global state (indigo_use_host_suffix, master/device tokens, adapters) is always restored, capture files are removed. I ran test_protocol_security: 23/23 pass, no .tmp left; test_agent_config (suffix off, '@Config test peers' catch-all): 56/56 pass. DEFECT (blocking): the change breaks an existing test that asserts the old containment routing. indigo_test/integration/system_alpaca/core_cases.h:1333 (core_proxy_names_without_at) expects a request for 'Focuser Simulator @ ' SA_SERVER_NAME ('... @ INDIGO Alpaca Simulator') to reach the adapter '@ INDIGO'; with exact suffix routing it no longer does. Ran: INDIGO_TEST_CASE_FILTER=core_proxy_names ./build/integration/test_system_alpaca_simulator -> 'core_cases.h:1333: check failed ... atomic_load(&core_remote_requests) == 1', FAIL core_proxy_names_without_at (the other three core_proxy_names cases pass). This test is opt-in (OPT_IN_DRIVER_TESTS) so flow check unit did not catch it, but it is par

Round 2: no defects. (1) Round-1 finding fixed: the positive control in indigo_test/integration/system_alpaca/core_cases.h:1334 now sends to 'Focuser @ Pier', which ends exactly with ' @ Pier' and reaches only the attached '@ Pier' (count == 1), under both old and exact routing; it still proves the counter works for a name that keeps its '@', so the preceding zero count for the real proxy names stays meaningful; the case is not weakened. Comments at core_cases.h:1300-1302 and indigo_drivers/system_alpaca/indigo_system_alpaca.c:323-326 now correctly describe exact suffix routing for change requests and containment for enumeration/BLOB mode (comment only, no version bump needed). (2) Session-device exemption (indigo_libs/indigo_bus.c:1011-1021) matches the owner decision: the exemption is applied before the loop condition is re-evaluated, so a session match leaves local false and the scan continues, and a later non-session device with the same name still sets it; the #if !defined(INDIGO_CLIENT) guard mirrors the attach/detach guards at indigo_bus.c:863-865 and 1427-1429 and uses the same column-0 preprocessor style; the comment above the scan is accurate. indigo_start attaches no other device, and the other library-internal attachments (indigo_client.c adapters, additional/slave devices in indigo_driver.c and indigo_filter.c) are not always-present, so no other device shadows a remote one by default. New case 'server request forwarded without host suffix' links full libindigo (session device 'Server' attached), so without the exemption the pre-scan would find 'Server' locally and the assertion would fail; it restores the master token and detaches its adapter. Ran: test_protocol_security 24/24 pass; the ASan/UBSan variant build/security/test_protocol_security all pass, no sanitizer reports; test_system_alpaca_simulator filtered to core_proxy_names 4/4 pass; libindigo_client.a rebuilt with no indigo_session_device reference. Workspace left clean. Out of scope for the ow

Owner approved the design on 2026-11-15 with option A only: make the remote-server routing in indigo_change_property exact (scenarios L1 and L3 in design.md). Option B is not approved: the server master token is still sent over server chains (scenario L2 stays as it is) and the '@ servername' ACL entry is neither implemented nor removed from the documentation. Not approved either: extending exact routing to indigo_enumerate_properties and indigo_enable_blob (design open question 4); report it, do not implement it. Reproduction on the unfixed tree (worktree based on master f9b1a34ed), new cases in indigo_test/unit/test_protocol_security.c with file-capturing XML client adapters (is_remote set, synthetic tokens). L1 confirmed: with indigo_use_host_suffix false, indigo_change_switch_property_1(NULL, 'Security', ...) reached the local device and was also written to adapter '@ Remote' as newSwitchVector device='Security' name='S' token=<local device token>, and after removing the device token again with token=<master token>. L3 confirmed: with the suffix on and adapters '@ host'/'@ host:7625' and '@ indigo'/'@ indigosky', a request for 'X @ host:7625' (resp. 'X @ indigosky') stamped with its device token was written to the right adapter and also to '@ host' (resp. '@ indigo') as device='X' token=<token of X @ host:7625>. Requests for 'X @ host' / 'X @ indigo' were not misrouted. Regression cases passed before the fix: suffix off request for 'RemoteOnly' forwarded with the master token (prop_tool path); suffix on network-client request (server-side XML adapter, client->is_remote true) for 'X @ Remote' relayed with the client's own token. Result: test_protocol_security 3 failed assertions in 2 cases, 21 passed.

After the fix (option A, indigo_change_property only): new static helper has_host_suffix() in indigo_libs/indigo_bus.c; with the suffix on a request goes to adapter '@ host' only when its device name ends exactly with ' @ host' (at least one character before the space); with the suffix off adapters get no request whose device name equals a local (non-'@') device. test_protocol_security: all 23 cases pass, including L1 (nothing for 'Security' written to '@ Remote', the local device still received both requests), L3 (requests for 'X @ host', 'X @ host:7625', 'X @ indigo', 'X @ indigosky' each written only to their own adapter, as device='X' with the device token), and the regressions (suffix-off 'RemoteOnly' still forwarded with the master token; network-client token relayed unchanged for 'X @ Remote'). flow check passed on tree fa90fbf2: whitespace and unit (80 unit executables, exit 0, no FAIL lines). Not changed, per owner decision: L2 (master token over server chains), the '@ servername' ACL entry, and the substring routing in indigo_enumerate_properties / indigo_enable_blob (still misroute for L3 naming, no tokens involved). No documentation in indigo_docs describes the substring routing, so no doc change; the comment in indigo_drivers/system_alpaca/indigo_system_alpaca.c:322-325 still describes containment routing, which remains true for enumerate/enable_blob; drivers were out of scope, left unchanged.

Review round 1 (changes) addressed. core_proxy_names_without_at passed on master's bus routing (temporary swap of indigo_bus.c in the worktree: 4/4 core_proxy_names cases passed) and failed with the fix because its positive control 'Focuser Simulator @ INDIGO Alpaca Simulator' reached adapter '@ INDIGO' only through the substring match. The control now sends to 'Focuser @ Pier' (the configured DeviceName with its '@' kept), which is routed to the attached '@ Pier' under both the old and the exact routing, so the case still proves that proxy names without '@' reach no remote service; comments in core_cases.h and the comment in indigo_drivers/system_alpaca/indigo_system_alpaca.c:322-326 now describe exact suffix routing for change requests and containment for enumeration/BLOB mode (comment only, no version bump). test_system_alpaca_simulator full run: before the adjustment 277 run, 276 passed, 1 failed (core_proxy_names_without_at); after 277 run, 277 passed. test_protocol_security all passed; test_agent_config 56/56 passed. flow check passed on tree 135def31 (whitespace, unit). OPEN ISSUE, not fixed: the design's statement that suffix-off processes host no colliding local devices is wrong for libindigo (non-INDIGO_CLIENT) builds: indigo_start() attaches the local session device 'Server' (indigo_session.c), so with indigo_use_host_suffix false a change request for the remote 'Server' device (Server.DRIVERS, LOAD, ...) is no longer forwarded to any remote server. Confirmed with a scratch in-process program linked against the worktree libindigo: master routing forwarded newSwitchVector device='Server' name='DRIVERS' to '@ Remote', the fixed routing sent nothing. indigo_prop_tool links libindigo_client (INDIGO_CLIENT, no session device) and is unaffected; indigo_test/integration/test_server_driver_stress.c (opt-in, suffix off, drives Server.DRIVERS of a spawned indigo_server through -lindigo) is affected by code reading but could not be exercised here: the worktree has n

The approved L1 fix (host suffix off: do not forward a request to remote servers when a local device has exactly that name) has a regression found in review round 2: a process built on full libindigo attaches a local session device named 'Server' (indigo_bus.c:863-864, indigo_session.c), so with the suffix off a request for 'Server' (for example Server.DRIVERS) is no longer forwarded to any remote server. Confirmed with a throwaway program: master forwards it to '@ Remote', the fixed routing sends nothing. indigo_prop_tool is not affected (libindigo_client has no session device); indigo_test/integration/test_server_driver_stress.c and third-party embedders are. Owner decision needed: (1) keep the L1 fix but leave the local session 'Server' device out of the local-name check, so 'Server' requests are still forwarded with the suffix off; (2) drop the L1 part and keep only the exact suffix routing (L3); (3) keep the fix as it is and accept the regression.

Owner decision 2026-11-15: option 1. Keep the L1 fix but leave the local session 'Server' device out of the local-name check, so with the host suffix off requests for 'Server' are still forwarded to remote servers as before. Accepted consequence: for the 'Server' device a locally stamped token can still reach remote servers when the suffix is off.

Owner confirmed on 2026-11-15, after the compatibility impact was explained, that both intended behaviour changes are accepted: with the host suffix on a request is routed only to the remote server whose name is the exact suffix of the device name, and with the suffix off a name that exists locally (other than the session 'Server' device) addresses only the local device (design open question 3).

Owner decision implemented: in indigo_change_property the local-name check (suffix off) skips the session device, identified by pointer (devices[i] != &indigo_session_device, declared in indigo/indigo_session.h which indigo_bus.c already includes), guarded by #if !defined(INDIGO_CLIENT) like the existing attach/detach of that device, since libindigo_client has no session device. New unit case 'server request forwarded without host suffix': before the exemption nothing was written to '@ Remote' for a 'Server' request (FAIL); after, newSwitchVector device='Server' name='S' token=<master token> is forwarded, which is the accepted consequence; the L1 case for local 'Security' still passes. Results on the final source: test_protocol_security 24/24 passed; test_agent_config 56/56 passed; test_system_alpaca_simulator 277 run, 277 passed, 0 failed. Both libindigo and libindigo_client built; indigo_prop_tool linked against libindigo_client.a (no session-device reference in the client indigo_bus.o). test_server_driver_stress (opt-in) run with a one-driver list generated by indigo_driver_metadata for indigo_system_alpaca (INDIGO_STRESS_DRIVERS=indigo_system_alpaca, cycles 2, iterations 3, seed 1, timeout 20 s): 3/3 passed; the same run with the exemption temporarily removed (cycles 1, iterations 1, timeout 10 s) failed 3/3 with 'server hung: no answer to loading indigo_system_alpaca', confirming the regression found in round 2 and its fix. flow check passed on tree d4fb5697 (whitespace, unit).

Not changed, per owner decision: L2 (master token over server chains), the '@ servername' ACL entry, and the substring routing in indigo_enumerate_properties / indigo_enable_blob (still misroute for L3 naming, no tokens involved). No documentation in indigo_docs describes the substring routing, so no doc change; the comment in indigo_drivers/system_alpaca/indigo_system_alpaca.c:322-325 still describes containment routing, which remains true for enumerate/enable_blob; drivers were out of scope, left unchanged.

Review round 1 (changes) addressed. core_proxy_names_without_at passed on master's bus routing (temporary swap of indigo_bus.c in the worktree: 4/4 core_proxy_names cases passed) and failed with the fix because its positive control 'Focuser Simulator @ INDIGO Alpaca Simulator' reached adapter '@ INDIGO' only through the substring match. The control now sends to 'Focuser @ Pier' (the configured DeviceName with its '@' kept), which is routed to the attached '@ Pier' under both the old and the exact routing, so the case still proves that proxy names without '@' reach no remote service; comments in core_cases.h and the comment in indigo_drivers/system_alpaca/indigo_system_alpaca.c:322-326 now describe exact suffix routing for change requests and containment for enumeration/BLOB mode (comment only, no version bump). test_system_alpaca_simulator full run: before the adjustment 277 run, 276 passed, 1 failed (core_proxy_names_without_at); after 277 run, 277 passed. test_protocol_security all passed; test_agent_config 56/56 passed. flow check passed on tree 135def31 (whitespace, unit). OPEN ISSUE, not fixed: the design's statement that suffix-off processes host no colliding local devices is wrong for libindigo (non-INDIGO_CLIENT) builds: indigo_start() attaches the local session device 'Server' (indigo_session.c), so with indigo_use_host_suffix false a change request for the remote 'Server' device (Server.DRIVERS, LOAD, ...) is no longer forwarded to any remote server. Confirmed with a scratch in-process program linked against the worktree libindigo: master routing forwarded newSwitchVector device='Server' name='DRIVERS' to '@ Remote', the fixed routing sent nothing. indigo_prop_tool links libindigo_client (INDIGO_CLIENT, no session device) and is unaffected; indigo_test/integration/test_server_driver_stress.c (opt-in, suffix off, drives Server.DRIVERS of a spawned indigo_server through -lindigo) is affected by code reading but could not be exercised here: the worktree has no driver list in build/share/indigo, so it fails with '0 of 0 drivers listed' independent of this change. Owner decision needed on how L1 should treat the session device.

Owner confirmed on 2026-11-15, after the compatibility impact was explained, that both intended behaviour changes are accepted: with the host suffix on a request is routed only to the remote server whose name is the exact suffix of the device name, and with the suffix off a name that exists locally (other than the session 'Server' device) addresses only the local device (design open question 3).

Owner decision implemented: in indigo_change_property the local-name check (suffix off) skips the session device, identified by pointer (devices[i] != &indigo_session_device, declared in indigo/indigo_session.h which indigo_bus.c already includes), guarded by #if !defined(INDIGO_CLIENT) like the existing attach/detach of that device, since libindigo_client has no session device. New unit case 'server request forwarded without host suffix': before the exemption nothing was written to '@ Remote' for a 'Server' request (FAIL); after, newSwitchVector device='Server' name='S' token=<master token> is forwarded, which is the accepted consequence; the L1 case for local 'Security' still passes. Results on the final source: test_protocol_security 24/24 passed; test_agent_config 56/56 passed; test_system_alpaca_simulator 277 run, 277 passed, 0 failed. Both libindigo and libindigo_client built; indigo_prop_tool linked against libindigo_client.a (no session-device reference in the client indigo_bus.o). test_server_driver_stress (opt-in) run with a one-driver list generated by indigo_driver_metadata for indigo_system_alpaca (INDIGO_STRESS_DRIVERS=indigo_system_alpaca, cycles 2, iterations 3, seed 1, timeout 20 s): 3/3 passed; the same run with the exemption temporarily removed (cycles 1, iterations 1, timeout 10 s) failed 3/3 with 'server hung: no answer to loading indigo_system_alpaca', confirming the regression found in round 2 and its fix. flow check passed on tree d4fb5697 (whitespace, unit).

questions.text: The approved L1 fix (host suffix off: do not forward a request to remote servers when a local device has exactly that name) has a regression found in review round 2: a process built on full libindigo attaches a local session device named 'Server' (indigo_bus.c:863-864, indigo_session.c), so with the suffix off a request for 'Server' (for example Server.DRIVERS) is no longer forwarded to any remote server. Confirmed with a throwaway program: master forwards it to '@ Remote', the fixed routing sends nothing. indigo_prop_tool is not affected (libindigo_client has no session device); indigo_test/integration/test_server_driver_stress.c and third-party embedders are. Owner decision needed: (1) keep the L1 fix but leave the local session 'Server' device out of the local-name check, so 'Server' requests are still forwarded with the suffix off; (2) drop the L1 part and keep only the exact suffix routing (L3); (3) keep the fix as it is and accept the regression.
questions.answer: Owner decision 2026-11-15: option 1. Keep the L1 fix but leave the local session 'Server' device out of the local-name check, so with the host suffix off requests for 'Server' are still forwarded to remote servers as before. Accepted consequence: for the 'Server' device a locally stamped token can still reach remote servers when the suffix is off.
